topic: Frontier-level AI running on a laptop, offline
angle: The privacy and cost argument changed the moment this became possible
hook: Frontier-class AI now runs on a laptop, offline
caption:
Running a serious model locally used to mean a server rack. It now means a well-specced laptop and an afternoon. That changes two arguments at once: what your AI costs, and where your data goes. For anyone handling client work under an NDA, the second one matters more than the first.

#localai #privacy #opensource #aitools #llm #technews

slides.text: Frontier-class AI now runs on a *laptop*, offline
slides.subline: No API key, no usage cap, no data leaving the machine

slides.text: Unplug the internet and the model keeps working. That single fact rewrites the cost and privacy argument.

slides.title: Why it matters for work
slides.body: Client contracts increasingly forbid pasting their material into a hosted AI. A local model is the only version of this that survives an NDA, and that unlocks work you currently cannot take.

slides.caption: what inference costs once the model lives on your own machine

slides.left_text: Per-token billing, a usage cap, and your prompts on someone else's server.
slides.right_text: Electricity. That is the whole running cost, and nothing leaves the laptop.

slides.title: The honest catch
slides.body: Local still loses to the best hosted models on the hardest reasoning, and it will eat your battery. Use it for volume, privacy and drafting. Keep a hosted key for the genuinely hard problems.

slides.text: Save this before you need it
slides.subline: Send it to someone still paying for this
